title: Boto Cor-de-Rosa
subtitle: Light a candle in memory of the departed.

trails.title: Urgent Need for Counseling
trails.description: He needs counseling, and whoever counsels him will also need it too.

content.text:
Below is a recording of the interrogation of a member of the Order of Enlightenment that occurred in San Francisco:

"Next, you will need to answer a few simple questions. This 'Order of Enlightenment' is just another front for Manus Vindictae, correct?"

"Ask whatever you like, I ain't gonna tell you anything, Foundation lapdog!"

"Please calm down. This doesn't have to be a hostile interrogation, but your answers here will influence our assessment of you. You know Arcana is dead, right?"

"Ignorant fool! The Guiding One's fate is always in her own hands! She chose a temporary death to suffer for us. One day, she will return, like an angel, and we will be reunited. We will once again become one, returning to that glorious age!"

"I have no intention of arguing with you. You're sweating profusely—do you need some water?"

"I won't drink anything you give me!!!"

"Alright, let's finish this quickly so you can return to your room and rest. Can you tell me who your current leader is? Is it 'Forget Me Not'? Or the former School of Apeiron arcanist Sophia? Or someone else?"

"How dare you call the Preacher by her name!!!"

"... You may go now. Please notify the next person ... Uh, never mind, I'll call them myself."

items.text: Boto Cor-de-Rosa
Sao Paulo Veterans' Residence

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: Oh, more visitors?
It's Lopera. She's safe.
But where's Sotheby?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank goodness. You survived, too. What about Sotheby?

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Oh, something happened in the favela earlier, so she decided to stay there. Don't worry. Duncan's with her.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We've got bad news. Dr. Dores has been abducted by the Brotherhood.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: What? Idiots! What's wrong with them?!

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Ugh, guess I'll call the base. My father will figure something out.

items.speaker: White Rum
items.text: Sink me! Lopera! I thought you'd been sent to Davy Jones's locker!
White Rum soars through the air and lands squarely in Lopera's arms.
The ferocity of the embrace is enough to knock a grown man to the ground.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Hahaha! Why did you think that? I'm tougher than the stubble on the chins of the old geezers here!

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: I'm like you, a ship that'll never sink!

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Umm, Timekeeper, who's that over there?
Kimberly is peeking out through the doorway, only a sliver of her face showing through the gap.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Kimberly? Did my father let you go?
She's been released?

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Oh, Timekeeper, let me explain. When we were routing out the deserters, we found Kimberly hanging out with the Manus thugs.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Pa took her off somewhere, and he always has a plan, so I didn't bother asking where she ended up.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Hey, come over here and say hi. When did Pa let you go?

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Or did you sneak out somehow?
Kimberly's eyes shift, her claws tensed, as if ready to spring into action at any moment.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I think ... Ms. Kimberly, didn't you pull me out of the water?

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: How did you know?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Shortly after my fever subsided, I started to remember what happened just before I lost consciousness.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There was a voice ringing in my head. It was you calling out to me, "Vertin, I can't have you dying here! You mustn't give up!"

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: What?! I did not say that! I just took you to the doctor and left!
Her protestation is almost a scream.

items.speaker: White Rum
items.text: Aye, 'tis true what Vertin says. Though Kimberly denies it, she chose to save her—even when she had plenty of chances to blow the lass down.

items.speaker: White Rum
items.text: She's a good lass at heart. Not an enemy, Lopera.
Lopera lowers her guard, offering a friendly wave to Kimberly.
Kimberly cautiously steps out of the doorway but maintains some distance between the two of them.
Lopera looks at her new "friend." Her attire has given her a totally different appearance.
After a brief pause, Lopera smiles at her.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: You have to understand, it's pretty hard not to suspect someone who hangs around with the Manus.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Anyway, I guess there must've been some kind of misunderstanding. Back then, I didn't have time to ... In any case, I'm sorry, Kimberly.
Lopera extends a hand in a gesture of peace, but Kimberly hesitates, her claws tensing once again.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: It's fine. But don't think I'll forgive you so easily.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Speaking of the Manus and the Brotherhood, I never quite understood what they were trying to do.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: I don't blame you. I still don't really get it, either.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: So you're really not in the same boat as them?
A sudden yet perfectly reasonable question.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Of course not! I don't have a boat, no, I mean, I'm not in any boat with anyone!

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: If only I'd found my ...
She looks around as if she's forgotten something but finds nothing.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Listen, I don't know who it is you're looking for, but it's not me. I've already told you everything I know. If I'm not welcome here, I'll get out of your way.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Just please don't take me back to that place. I don't want to see that thing ever again.
She refuses to look at the weapons around Lopera's waist. Perhaps in a restrained sense of rejection or fear, or something hidden deep within her heart.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: Alright, girls. If you want to have a chat, at least take a seat first.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: It simply won't do to have you all standing around the entrance like this.
Mamãe Mariana takes Kimberly with one hand and Lopera with the other and leads them back to the courtyard. When they arrive, she lays out some paçoca for them to snack on.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Eating candy's bad for your teeth, Grandma.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: Oh, I'm much too old to worry about that. When you reach my age, and just waking up each day is a blessing, you'll eat whatever you want, too.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mamãe Mariana, could I have a word with you, please? I have some questions about Mr. Duncan.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: Oh, Duncan, what kind of trouble has he stirred up now? Alright then. Why don't we head inside and give those two some space?

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: And Lopera, apologize to that poor girl properly, you hear?
Every lost friend is worth remembering.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: My father released you, which means you can be trusted.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: And you saved Vertin's life, too. I guess I shouldn't have been so hostile toward you.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Here, have a drink, as a token of my apology.
She hands her a warm cup of something dark. It has a rich smell.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: It's Salvadoran coffee. Great if you need to pull an all-nighter!
Kimberly raises the cup to her mouth with both hands and curiously sticks her tongue into the liquid.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Bleh! It's so bitter!

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Yep. Bitter like the old days.
Lopera falls silent for a while.
Kimberly glances at the gun around Lopera's waist.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: You know, back in Colombia, my father did horrible things to his plantation workers.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Well, my biological father. Not Igor.
Lopera looks off into the sky and laughs resignedly. It's as if she just spoke of a stranger rather than her flesh and blood.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: He said, "No, that's not the sound of gunfire outside. The workers are setting off fireworks. They're celebrating."

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: But they weren't fireworks. He betrayed his workers—his compatriots. It wasn't a celebration; it was a massacre.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: After that, I ran away from home. One day, the admiral and Molly found me. That's how I joined Zeno.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Betrayal's as common as dirt here. Comrades, friends, family, anyone could sell you out, and for cheap, too.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: I hope you can find your boat soon. You know, a place where people have your back.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Umm, can I not drink this?

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Hahahaha, of course. Don't force yourself. I know the taste isn't for everyone.
She clinks cups with her new friend.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Carlotta Lopez Rivera.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: That's my full name. Bit of a mouthful, huh?
Lopera stretches out her arm, closes one eye, and lines up the moon between her fingers. She closes her fist but catches nothing but the air.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: I wanted to erase it from my profile, from everywhere, to be honest, but my father disapproved.
She fiddles with her fingers, her eyes lingering on that unattainable celestial body.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Molly agreed with him. She said, "You mustn't forget your past, Pera."

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: So I let it go. But "Lopera" sounds so much nicer, so I prefer to go by that.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: And you, Kimberly? What's your real name?
Kimberly hesitates.

items.speaker: Anjo Nala
items.text: Nala. Nala Hari. The residents of Heartfelt Home called me Anjo Nala.
Guest Room, Veterans' Residence

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How long ago did Mr. Duncan move here? Do you remember?

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: It must have been ... five, maybe six years ago? I'm not entirely sure.
Five or six years ago. Nowhere near the '20s. What's going on?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do you have any photos of him?
Mariana nods and pulls a photograph from the storage room.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: We do have one, but it's been gathering dust for years. Let me see. Ah. Here. This is him.
She points to the man who looks like Mr. Karson.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I knew a gentleman who looked just like him.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: His name was Karson. Did Mr. Duncan ever go by that name?
The old woman blows the dust off the frame.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: No, not that any of us are aware of anyway. And I've known him since I was a medic in the army.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: Back then, people called him "Duncan the Dauntless" or "The All-Powerful Duncan." I never once heard "Karson" or anything of the like.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: Sorry I couldn't be of more help, my dear.
It seems an in-person meeting with Mr. Duncan is in order.
As they head outside, black flashes across their vision as a crow swoops down from above.
It releases the letter clutched in its claws.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A crow?
The crow perches nearby as the letter flutters down and lands at their feet.
The old woman picks it up and breaks the seal.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: Oh, dear. This looks like bad news.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Santos.
It's a cleanly written ransom note, signed "Santos."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Dr. Dores is being held captive in the colonel's manor.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He's given us three days.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He says that if Zeno doesn't return the deserters they detained, he'll execute the doctor.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mamãe Mariana, please contact Admiral Igor. We need Zeno's help.
TO BE CONTINUED…
